notes: Fiscal-year mapping: Johnson Controls reports fiscal years ended September 30; historical years used are FY2023 (ended Sep 30, 2023), FY2024, and FY2025 (ended Sep 30, 2025). ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2025/fy2025-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))

EBIT definition used for the historical/valuation package: EBIT = Income from continuing operations before income taxes + Net financing charges (both from Consolidated Statements of Income). This excludes interest via add-back of net financing charges and includes equity income as presented. ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2025/fy2025-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))

D&A and capex: D&A taken from cash flow adjustment line 'Depreciation and amortization'; capex taken from 'Capital expenditures' (absolute values). ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2025/fy2025-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))

NWC construction (historical): NWC computed as (Current assets − Cash and cash equivalents − Current assets held for sale) − (Current liabilities − Short-term debt − Current portion of long-term debt − Current liabilities held for sale), based on balance-sheet line items. This is a normalized operating NWC concept consistent with how management defines working-capital exclusions in earlier filings; sign can be negative. ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2024/fy2024-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))

NWC forecast: normalized NWC-to-sales ratio set to 0.002 (0.2%) for FY2026–FY2030 as a stabilization assumption post-portfolio actions; actual future NWC could differ materially. ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2025/fy2025-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))

Tax rate: modeled as a normalized effective tax rate of 0.10 for base case; continuing-ops effective tax rate was volatile due to discrete/benefit items in the historical window. ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2025/fy2025-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))

WACC is an explicit model input (0.085) rather than a sourced rate; it is a placeholder assumption for the DCF run and should be re-estimated if your pipeline uses a different capital structure or cost-of-capital framework.

Cash and debt are taken from FY2025 (Sep 30, 2025) balance sheet/capitalization disclosures and may not match March 2026 levels. ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2025/fy2025-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))
Current price: set to 129.7 USD based on the latest available trade timestamp from the market data lookup (trade time shown as Mar 20 UTC).

NOL balance: modeled from disclosed available net operating loss carryforwards of approx. $26.1 billion at Sep 30, 2025; NOL utilization percent is set to 0.80 as a modeling input (actual utilization depends on jurisdictional constraints and projected profitability). ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2025/fy2025-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))

Comps: EV/NTM Revenue, EV/NTM EBITDA, and P/E NTM were not reliably obtained from primary/official sources in this build; those fields are set to null and should be populated with your preferred market-data terminal outputs.

catalysts: Continued order/backlog momentum translating into sustained organic growth and margin expansion through FY2026. ([d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net](https://d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net/CIK-0000833444/4dea423c-4849-461e-bbdc-384eb0d819a6.pdf))

Successful execution of portfolio simplification actions without margin/working-capital dislocation. ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2025/fy2025-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))

Further guidance raises (or tangible free cash flow conversion upside) could re-rate expectations. ([d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net](https://d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net/CIK-0000833444/4dea423c-4849-461e-bbdc-384eb0d819a6.pdf))
company_overview: Johnson Controls is a global leader in building technology and services, including commercial HVAC equipment, controls, security, fire detection and suppression, and digital/smart building solutions via OpenBlue. ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2025/fy2025-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))

The business includes both products/systems and services revenue streams (maintenance, repair, retrofit, and monitoring). ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2025/fy2025-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))

On July 31, 2025, it completed the divestiture of the Residential and Light Commercial HVAC business to Bosch, with the sold business reflected as discontinued operations/held for sale in filings. ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2025/fy2025-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))
current_context: In fiscal Q1 2026, sales increased 7% (organic +6%) to ~$5.8 billion, with Q1 orders +39% organically and backlog of $18.2 billion (+20% organically). ([d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net](https://d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net/CIK-0000833444/4dea423c-4849-461e-bbdc-384eb0d819a6.pdf))

Management raised fiscal 2026 full-year continuing operations guidance: organic sales growth expected in mid-single digits (unchanged) and adjusted EPS ~$4.70 (previously ~$4.55). ([d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net](https://d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net/CIK-0000833444/4dea423c-4849-461e-bbdc-384eb0d819a6.pdf))

The setup remains driven by improving execution and margin expansion alongside continued order/backlog strength. ([d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net](https://d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net/CIK-0000833444/4dea423c-4849-461e-bbdc-384eb0d819a6.pdf))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth assumes sustained mid-single-digit organic momentum consistent with FY2026 guidance. ([d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net](https://d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net/CIK-0000833444/4dea423c-4849-461e-bbdc-384eb0d819a6.pdf))

EBIT margin recovery is modeled from historical volatility (restructuring/portfolio simplification) toward a normalized target margin by FY2030. ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2025/fy2025-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))

Capital intensity is kept roughly stable using historical depreciation and capex as a percent of sales (D&A ~3.6% of sales; capex ~2.0%). ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2025/fy2025-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))

Working capital intensity is modeled as broadly stable after major portfolio actions, using a normalized NWC-to-sales ratio. ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2024/fy2024-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))
key_risks: Execution risk: restructuring/transition costs or project timing shocks could pressure earnings and EBIT margins. ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2025/fy2025-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))

Demand and macro risk across end markets (commercial/industrial/data center/service cycles) could slow organic sales growth. ([d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net](https://d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net/CIK-0000833444/4dea423c-4849-461e-bbdc-384eb0d819a6.pdf))

Foreign exchange, commodity/input cost volatility, and pension-related cash impacts could affect operating cash flow. ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2025/fy2025-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))

Tax volatility (including discrete items) could cause effective tax rate deviations from modeled assumptions. ([investors.johnsoncontrols.com](https://investors.johnsoncontrols.com/~/media/Files/J/Johnson-Controls-IR-V2/quarterly-reports/2025/fy2025-form-10-k-jci-plc.pdf))
